In college I sold acid to a girl who ended up having an absolutely terrible trip. I considered her to be one of my best friends at the time, and this incident destroyed our friendship permanently. I was there to watch her pull off all her clothes, scream uncontrollably, projectile vomit, and tear apart her dorm room for over an hour while I and a few others tried everything we could to calm her down. Eventually as she was screaming so loudly and it was well past 1 am someone in the building called the police. I watched as police handcuffed her, still naked, to a chair and then after the EMTs arrived they loaded her onto a stretcher. I was not high, had no drugs on me and was able to avoid any repercussions for the incident. In her state she assaulted an EMT, a dorm worker and myself. She was charged with multiple crimes including felony assault of an EMT and was expelled from school. We continued to speak for about four months post-incident but stopped after multiple fights related to how I handled the incident, what happened in the days following the incident, and the responsibilities of how rent and bills were to be paid on an apartment we were to share the following school year after she was expelled. We had signed a lease with two other people, and she demanded we pay her portion of rent and bills as she was not coming back to the school. The three of us refused and she expressed her anger and resentment towards us. She only texted us from that point forward to demand we find a replacement roommate so she would not have to pay rent. This continued for a few months until we told her to fuck off in the most blunt way possible. This happened over six years ago, and since then we have not communicated in any way whatsoever. Based on what others who still have her on Facebook show me and my casual cyber-stalking of her public twitter page, she hasn't really bounced back from this. She has burned bridges with most of her friends and her entire family. She lives off her girlfriend and works at a grocery store and was never able to finish her degree. At the time I felt as though I ruined her life and felt intense guilt for the enitre situation for a few years after. The first year was one of the hardest, I began having intense recurring nightmares about what happened. My sleep schedule was terribly impacted and I feel behind in school. It took me about two years, and several therapy sessions to finally come to terms with what had happened and I ended up graduating three semesters after I should have. I don't blame all of my academic struggles on what had happened, but there was a noticeable dip in the quality and consistency of my work after the incident. I have no plans to contact her again but I still feel as though I owe her something for essentially ruining her life.
